seoTitle: Free DNS Zone File Parser: BIND Zone to Record Table
metaDescription: Parse a BIND zone file into a table of names, TTLs, classes, types and data. Handles $ORIGIN, $TTL, parentheses and @. Runs offline.
intro: Reads a BIND-style zone file and lists every record with its full name, TTL, class, type and data. It applies $ORIGIN and $TTL, joins multi-line records in parentheses and can print JSON.
why:
Zone files are compact on purpose: a blank owner repeats the previous name, @ means the origin, and names without a trailing dot get the origin added. That makes them hard to read and easy to get wrong, for example by forgetting a dot.

The parser expands all of that so you can see what a server would load. It checks a few common mistakes (missing SOA, a CNAME next to other data). It does not support $INCLUDE or $GENERATE, and it does not validate record data.
howTo: Add an origin if the file has no $ORIGIN line.
Read the table, or tick JSON for a machine-readable list.
Check the notes below the table for missing SOA records or CNAME conflicts.

faq.q: Why does a name end with a dot?
faq.a: A trailing dot marks a fully qualified name. The parser shows every owner name in that form.

faq.q: What if a record has no TTL?
faq.a: It uses the last $TTL, or the last explicit TTL in the file. If neither exists the TTL shows as a dash.
No. They are listed as not processed.

faq.q: Does it check that the data is valid?
faq.a: No. A type is checked against a list of known types, but the data is only split into fields.
